claims.text: A stable nanocrystalline solid-solution microstructure governs resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in high-entropy alloys.
High entropy of mixing suppresses the formation of deleterious intermetallic phases.
A stable nanocrystalline solid-solution microstructure promotes sluggish diffusion kinetics.
Suppressing deleterious intermetallic phases improves resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion.
Sluggish diffusion kinetics improves resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion.
Mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering produce the proposed nanocrystalline solid-solution mediator.
The proposed high-entropy alloy will have better simultaneous wear-and-corrosion resistance than conventional alloys of similar composition.
The prediction applies in harsh corrosive mechanical environments.
The prediction is limited to high-entropy alloys retaining a stable nanocrystalline solid-solution microstructure.
The exact relationship between entropy of mixing and wear-corrosion resistance is not fully understood.
